audits.title: 196 AN AUDIT OF PROTON-PUMP INHIBITOR PRESCRIBING IN PATIENTS ATTENDING A RAPID ACCESS FRAILTY ASSESSMENT UNIT
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on PPI prescribing indications
audits.setting: Rapid Access Frailty Assessment Unit, Midland Regional Hospital Tullamore

cycle1.result: 63 (52.5%) prescribed a PPI; only 15 (23.8%) had a documented indication in line with NICE.

audits.other_findings: Only one record mentioned PPI for iatrogenic gastritis despite gastro-erosive drugs; no records mentioned deprescribing.
audits.citation: McDonnell E, Corcoran L, Donnelly T. 196 AN AUDIT OF PROTON-PUMP INHIBITOR PRESCRIBING IN PATIENTS ATTENDING A RAPID ACCESS FRAILTY ASSESSMENT UNIT. Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac218.169.

audits.title: 193 Audit on Inappropriate Prescribing of Proton Pump Inhibitors Amongst Patients over 65 Years in an Acute Rehabilitation Hospital
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on indications for PPI use
audits.setting: Acute rehabilitation hospital (Royal Hospital Donnybrook, Dublin); patients over 65

cycle1.result: 43% on a PPI; 83.4% of these had no indication; 77.7% on therapeutic dose without indication; 100% on PPI longer than 6 weeks.

audits.intervention: Education to hospital doctors on NICE PPI prescribing guidelines.

cycle2.result: 60.4% on a PPI; 55% had no indication; 83% on PPI longer than 6 weeks; 56.5% on inappropriate dose.

audits.other_findings: Authors report inappropriate prescribing fell by 28.4% and accurate dosing improved by 21.2%.
audits.citation: O' Reilly E, Gopaul A, Cogan L. 193 Audit on Inappropriate Prescribing of Proton Pump Inhibitors Amongst Patients over 65 Years in an Acute Rehabilitation Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.114.

audits.title: 108 A Prospective Audit and Review of Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) in Older Adults in a Reablement Unit
audits.standard: PPI prescribing guidelines on indication and dose
audits.setting: 24-bed reablement unit, Our Lady's Hospice and Care Services, Dublin
audits.intervention: Pharmacist review with recommendations to the medical team: 8 (42.1%) dose reduced, 5 (26.3%) discontinued.
audits.other_findings: 6 (31.6%) inappropriate PPIs unsuitable for review due to bleed risk, ongoing reflux or other reasons.
audits.citation: Byrne A, Hizza Hila Ludin N, Byrne S, Purcell R. 108 A Prospective Audit and Review of Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) in Older Adults in a Reablement Unit. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.63.

audits.title: Prescribing of proton-pump inhibitors: auditing the management and reasons for prescribing in Danish general practice.
audits.setting: General practices in the Region of Southern Denmark (Audit Project Odense)

cycle1.result: PPIs taken >2 years in 58% and daily in 64%; appropriate reason in three of four patients; no gastroscopy in 46%; 25% had a PPI consultation within the last year.

audits.other_findings: 51 GPs and 47 staff participated; substantial variability between GPs in management.
audits.citation: Jarbøl DE, Lykkegaard J, Hansen JM, Munck A, Haastrup PF. Prescribing of proton-pump inhibitors: auditing the management and reasons for prescribing in Danish general practice. Fam Pract. 2019;36(6):758-764. doi:10.1093/fampra/cmz025. PMID: 31165863.

audits.title: Audit of PPI Prescribing Practices: A Risk to Patient Safety?
audits.standard: Consensus guideline on indications for PPI use (Scarpignato et al, 2016)
audits.setting: Department of General Surgery, Wexford General Hospital; surgical inpatients

cycle1.result: 73% were on PPI therapy; 30% had a documented indication concordant with recommendations; 70% of PPI prescriptions were inappropriate.

audits.title: Unexplained abdominal pain as a driver for inappropriate therapeutics: an audit on the use of intravenous proton pump inhibitors.
audits.standard: Hospital guidelines for intravenous PPI indication, dose and duration
audits.setting: Tertiary teaching hospital (University Malaya Medical Centre), adult inpatients

cycle1.result: Intravenous PPI was inappropriately prescribed for indication, dose or duration in 56/106 (52.8%) patients.

audits.intervention: Pharmacy interventions on individual incorrect prescriptions during the audit; no re-audit reported.
audits.other_findings: Unexplained abdominal pain drove 81 (76.4%) prescriptions; only 50/106 (47.2%) had endoscopy or surgery; interventions were accepted most when made by senior doctors (100%) versus clinical pharmacists (50%) and inpatient pharmacists (37.5%, p = 0.027).
audits.citation: Lai PS, Wong YY, Low YC, Lau HL, Chin KF, Mahadeva S. Unexplained abdominal pain as a driver for inappropriate therapeutics: an audit on the use of intravenous proton pump inhibitors. PeerJ. 2014;2:e451. doi:10.7717/peerj.451. PMID: 25024919.

audits.title: Audit of IV pantoprazole: pattern of administration and compliance with guideline in a teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Hospital guideline for intravenous pantoprazole indication and dosage (established during the study)

cycle1.result: Rate, indication and dosage of IV pantoprazole administration recorded before the guideline; figures not given in the abstract.

audits.intervention: A hospital guideline for IV pantoprazole was established.

cycle2.result: Guideline significantly reduced the rate of IV pantoprazole administration (P = 0.00) and cost (301,289,000 Rials or 8608 USD over 3 months), but did not correct indications and dosage at the same rate.

audits.other_findings: 400 randomly selected patients in total across both periods; stress ulcer prophylaxis was the most frequent approved indication and adherence to the guideline declined over time.
audits.citation: Moradi M, Raeesi S, Sepehri Z. Audit of IV pantoprazole: pattern of administration and compliance with guideline in a teaching hospital. Springerplus. 2016;5(1):1749. doi:10.1186/s40064-016-3428-2. PMID: 27795892.
